sections.partTitle: 第二部分 阅读（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共15小题；每小题2分，满分30分）阅读下列短文，从每题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中选出最佳选项。

passages.label: A
passages.text:
Each ARTS FIRST festival is a unique annual celebration of the Harvard community's artistic creativity. We invite you to join us for the coming ARTS FIRST. We look forward to welcoming you as we showcase the creativity of the Harvard arts community through performances, art exhibitions and art-making activities. The festival is a public event for Harvard and community members of all ages.

Light Awash in Watercolor
Learn about the materials and qualities of watercolor paint with experts from the Harvard Art Museums Materials Lab. Try your hand at some of the painting tricks used by artists whose works will be in the upcoming exhibition of American Watercolors 1880-1990: Into the Light.

Spineless Artists: Invertebrate Creativity
From webs to cocoons, invertebrates (无脊椎动物) create some of nature's most delicate and beautiful designs. Join Javier Marin from the Harvard Museum of Natural History to learn how insects and other invertebrates dance, inspire fashion and create art, while making your own spineless artists out of craft (手工艺) materials.

Wheel Throwing
Join instructors from the Ceramics Program and great potters from Quincy, Cabot and Mather Houses for demonstrations using the potter's wheel. Then create your own masterpiece!

Knitting and Pom-Pom Making
Join the Harvard Undergraduate Knitting Circle to make pom-poms and tassels out of thread, or pick up a pair of needles and learn to knit (编织).

passages.label: B
passages.text:
Animals can express their needs using a lot of ways. For instance, almost all animals have distinct vocals (声音) that they rely on to either ask for help, scare away any dangerous animals or look for shelter. But cats are special creatures who possess amazing vocalization skills. They are able to have entire conversations with humans using meows and you're able to interpret it. If a pet cat is hungry, it will keep meowing to attract attention and find food. However, when a cat is looking for affection, they tend to produce stretched and soft meows. Meowing starts as soon as a baby cat is brought to life and uses it to get the mother's attention and be fed.

Cats have many heightened senses, but their sense of smell is quite impressive. They use their noses to assess their environment and look out for any signs of danger. They will sniff out specific areas before they choose a place to relax. However, another way the cats are able to distinguish between situations is by looking for familiar smells. Your cat will likely smell your face and store the smell in its memory and use it to recognize you in the future. That's why most pet cats are able to tell immediately if their owners were around any other cats, which they don't usually like.

Dogs are known for their impressive fetching habit, but cats take this behavior up a notch. Many cats will find random objects outside and bring them to their owners. This is a very old habit that's been present in all kinds of predators (食肉动物). Cats bring gifts for their owners to show they love you. These adorable little hunters are just doing something that it's been in their nature since the beginning of time. So just go along with it!

passages.label: C
passages.text:
The Saint Lukas train doesn't accept passengers — it accepts only the sick. The Saint Lukas is one of five government-sponsored medical trains that travel to remote towns in central and eastern Russia. Each stop lasts an average of two days, and during that time the doctors and nurses on board provide rural (乡村) populations with basic medical care, X-ray scans and prescriptions.

"People started queuing to make an appointment early in the morning," says Emile Ducke, a German photographer who traveled with the staff of the Saint Lukas for a two-week trip in November through the vast regions (区域) of Krasnoyarsk and Khakassia.

Russia's public health care service has been in serious need of modernization. The government has struggled to come up with measures to address the problem, particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River, including arranging doctor's appointments by video chat and expanding financial aid programs to motivate doctors to practice medicine in remote parts of the country like Krasnoyarsk.

The annual arrival of the Saint Lukas is another attempt to improve the situation. For 10 months every year, the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock (补给). Then it starts all over again the next month. Most stations wait about a year between visits.

Doctors see up to 150 patients every day. The train's equipment allows for basic checkups. "I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants working and living in such little space but still staying focused and very concerned," says Ducke. "They were the best chance for many rural people to get the treatment they want."

passages.label: D
passages.text:
"I didn't like the ending," I said to my favorite college professor. It was my junior year of undergraduate, and I was doing an independent study on Victorian literature. I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was heartbroken with the ending. Prof. Gracie, with all his patience, asked me to think about it beyond whether I liked it or not. He suggested I think about the difference between endings that I wanted for the characters and endings that were right for the characters, endings that satisfied the story even if they didn't have a traditionally positive outcome. Of course, I would have preferred a different ending for Tom and Maggie Tulliver, but the ending they got did make the most sense for them.

This was an aha moment for me, and I never thought about endings the same way again. From then on, if I wanted to read an ending guaranteed to be happy, I'd pick up a love romance. If I wanted an ending I couldn't guess, I'd pick up a mystery (悬疑小说). One where I kind of knew what was going to happen, historical fiction. Choosing what to read became easier.

But writing the end — that's hard. It's hard for writers because endings carry so much weight with readers. You have to balance creating an ending that's unpredictable, but doesn't seem to come from nowhere, one that fits what's right for the characters.

That's why this issue (期) of Writer's Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending for whatever kind of writing you're doing. If it's short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques you can try to see which one helps you stick the landing. Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels to see what key points they include and how you can adapt them for your work.

This issue won't tell you what your ending should be — that's up to you and the story you're telling — but it might provide what you need to get there.

questions.stem: What do we know about ARTS FIRST?

options.text: It is an exhibition of oil paintings.
It offers art courses for all ages.
It is a major tourist attraction.

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜本文是应用文，介绍哈佛 ARTS FIRST 艺术节的四项活动。
explanation.question: 问关于 ARTS FIRST 我们可以得知什么。
explanation.evidence: we showcase the creativity of the Harvard arts community through performances, art exhibitions and art-making activities
explanation.answer: C。艺术节通过演出、展览和手工创作等活动展示创造力，属于休闲娱乐性活动。它不限于油画展（A），也不是课程（B），文中未提旅游景点（D）。

questions.stem: Which program will you join if you're interested in drawing pictures?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜四个项目的内容对应。
explanation.question: 问如果对画画感兴趣该参加哪个项目。
explanation.evidence: Light Awash in Watercolor: Learn about the materials and qualities of watercolor paint…Try your hand at some of the painting tricks
explanation.answer: A。只有第一个项目涉及水彩颜料与绘画技巧。B 是做手工，C 是陶艺拉坯，D 是编织。

questions.stem: What can you do together with Javier Marin?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜Javier Marin 负责的项目内容。
explanation.question: 问可以和 Javier Marin 一起做什么。
explanation.evidence: Join Javier Marin…while making your own spineless artists out of craft materials.
explanation.answer: B。用手工材料做自己的“无脊椎艺术家”，即做手工。文中的 dance 是讲无脊椎动物如何“舞动”，不是人跳传统舞，故 A 错。

questions.stem: What can be learned about cats' meowing from the first paragraph?

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜本文是说明文，介绍猫的三种行为（叫声、嗅觉、叼东西）。
explanation.question: 问从第一段可以得知猫的叫声有什么特点。
explanation.evidence: Meowing starts as soon as a baby cat is brought to life and uses it to get the mother's attention and be fed…If a pet cat is hungry, it will keep meowing to attract attention and find food.
explanation.answer: A。小猫一出生就会叫，用叫声引起母猫注意以获得喂食，饿了也靠叫声觅食，可见喵叫是一种生存技能。叫声天生并非母猫所教（B），且文中说人能听懂（C 与原文相反）。

questions.stem: How does a pet cat assess different situations?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜第二段关于嗅觉的说明。
explanation.question: 问宠物猫如何判断不同的情境。
explanation.evidence: They use their noses to assess their environment…another way the cats are able to distinguish between situations is by looking for familiar smells.
explanation.answer: C。猫用鼻子评估环境、通过寻找熟悉的气味来分辨情境，即靠气味判断。

questions.stem: Which best explains the phrase "take...up a notch" in paragraph 3?

explanation.summary: 词句猜测题｜第三段狗与猫的对比。
explanation.question: 问第三段短语 take...up a notch 的含义。
explanation.evidence: Dogs are known for their impressive fetching habit, but cats take this behavior up a notch. Many cats will find random objects outside and bring them to their owners.
explanation.answer: D。狗以叼取见长，but 转折说猫把这一行为“更上一层”——不仅叼回来，还把外面捡到的东西当礼物送给主人，故意为“做得更好”。

questions.stem: What is a suitable title for the text?

options.text: Tips on Finding a Smart Cat
How to Keep Your Cat Healthy

explanation.summary: 标题归纳题｜全文三段结构。
explanation.question: 问本文合适的标题是什么。
explanation.evidence: 三段分别解释猫为什么喵叫、如何用嗅觉判断环境、为什么叼东西送主人。
explanation.answer: B。全文逐段解读猫的典型行为及其含义，故“读懂你的猫的行为”最贴切。文中没有挑选聪明猫（A）、玩乐（C）或健康养护（D）的内容。

questions.stem: How is the Saint Lukas different from other trains?

options.text: It reserves seats for the seniors.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜本文是新闻报道，介绍俄罗斯的医疗列车 Saint Lukas。
explanation.question: 问 Saint Lukas 与其他列车有何不同。
explanation.evidence: The Saint Lukas train doesn't accept passengers — it accepts only the sick…the doctors and nurses on board provide rural populations with basic medical care, X-ray scans and prescriptions.
explanation.answer: C。它不载普通乘客，只接收病人，车上医生护士提供基础诊疗、X 光和处方，功能相当于一所医院。

questions.stem: What can we infer from paragraph 3 about Krasnoyarsk?

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜第三段对偏远地区医疗状况的描述。
explanation.question: 问从第三段可以推断出关于 Krasnoyarsk 的什么信息。
explanation.evidence: particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River…expanding financial aid programs to motivate doctors to practice medicine in remote parts of the country like Krasnoyarsk
explanation.answer: D。政府需靠扩大资助来吸引医生去 Krasnoyarsk 这类偏远地区执业，说明当地医疗资源匮乏、需要援助。

questions.stem: How long can the Saint Lukas work with one supply?

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜第四段的运行周期。
explanation.question: 问 Saint Lukas 一次补给能工作多久。
explanation.evidence: the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock
explanation.answer: D。列车两周内停靠约八站，然后才返回州府加油补给，故一次补给可工作约两周。10 个月是每年的运行时长（B 干扰），约一年是同一站两次到访的间隔（A 干扰）。

questions.stem: What is Ducke's attitude toward the Saint Lukas' services?

explanation.summary: 观点态度题｜末段 Ducke 的原话。
explanation.question: 问 Ducke 对 Saint Lukas 提供的服务持何态度。
explanation.evidence: I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants…They were the best chance for many rural people to get the treatment they want.
explanation.answer: A。“非常敬佩”“是许多乡村居民获得治疗的最好机会”都是正面评价，故为赞赏的态度。

questions.stem: Why did the author go to Prof. Gracie?

options.text: To ask for a reading list.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜本文是杂志刊首语，从一次师生对话谈如何写好结尾。
explanation.question: 问作者为什么去找 Gracie 教授。
explanation.evidence: "I didn't like the ending," I said to my favorite college professor…I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was heartbroken with the ending.
explanation.answer: A。作者刚读完《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》，因不满结尾去找教授探讨，即讨论一部小说。

questions.stem: What did the author realize after seeing Gracie?

options.text: Writing is a matter of personal preferences.
Readers are often carried away by character.
Each type of literature has its unique end.
A story which begins well will end well.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜第二段的“顿悟”。
explanation.question: 问见过 Gracie 之后作者意识到了什么。
explanation.evidence: if I wanted to read an ending guaranteed to be happy, I'd pick up a love romance. If I wanted an ending I couldn't guess, I'd pick up a mystery. One where I kind of knew what was going to happen, historical fiction.
explanation.answer: C。作者据此把言情、悬疑、历史小说与各自的结尾类型对应起来，即认识到每种文学体裁都有其独特的结尾方式。

questions.stem: What is expected of a good ending?

options.text: It fits with the story development.

explanation.summary: 细节理解题｜第一段教授的观点与第三段的呼应。
explanation.question: 问一个好的结尾应该做到什么。
explanation.evidence: endings that satisfied the story even if they didn't have a traditionally positive outcome…an ending that's unpredictable, but doesn't seem to come from nowhere, one that fits what's right for the characters
explanation.answer: B。好结尾要契合故事本身与人物的走向，而不是迎合读者喜好（A）；教授明确指出结尾未必是传统意义上的圆满（C 错）。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention Peter Mountford and Elizabeth Sims?

options.text: To give examples of great novelists.
To stress the theme of this issue.
To encourage writing for the magazine.

explanation.summary: 推理判断题｜第四段举例的作用。
explanation.question: 问作者提到 Peter Mountford 和 Elizabeth Sims 的目的是什么。
explanation.evidence: this issue of Writer's Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending…Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques…Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels
explanation.answer: B。两人分别拆解写结尾的技巧和名著末章，是用来说明本期“如何写好结尾”这一主题的具体内容，起强调主题的作用。

sections.partTitle: 第二部分 阅读（共两节，满分40分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共5小题；每小题2分，满分10分）根据短文内容，从短文后的选项中选出能填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

pool.text: We don't always eat just to satisfy hunger.
Don't swallow a meal on the way to work.
Most of us need to double the amount we eat.
Instead, surround yourself with healthy choices.
For many of us, moderation means eating less than we do now.
That won't lead to cheating or giving up on your new eating plan.

passages.label: E
passages.text:
What is moderation (适度)? Basically, it means eating only as much food as your body needs. You should feel satisfied at the end of a meal, but not too full. ____36____ But it doesn't mean saying goodbye to the foods you love.

Take your time. It's important to slow down and think about food as something nutritious rather than just something to eat in between meetings. ____37____ It actually takes a few minutes for your brain to tell your body that it has had enough food, so eat slowly and stop eating before you feel full.

Eat with others whenever possible. Eating alone, especially in front of the TV or computer, often leads to mindless overeating. And be careful about the foods you keep at hand. It's more challenging to eat in moderation if you have unhealthy snacks at the ready, like cookies. ____38____

Control emotional (情绪) eating. ____39____ Many of us also turn to food to deal with unpleasant emotions such as sadness, loneliness, or boredom. But by learning healthier ways to manage emotions, you can regain control over the food you eat and your feelings.

____40____ A healthy breakfast can start your metabolism (新陈代谢), while eating small, healthy meals keeps your energy up all day. Avoid eating late at night. Try to eat dinner earlier and fast for 14—16 hours until breakfast the next morning. Studies suggest that eating only when you're most active and giving your digestive system a long break each day may help to regulate weight.

options.text: We don't always eat just to satisfy hunger.
Don't swallow a meal on the way to work.
Most of us need to double the amount we eat.
Instead, surround yourself with healthy choices.
For many of us, moderation means eating less than we do now.
That won't lead to cheating or giving up on your new eating plan.

explanation.summary: 七选五｜本文是说明文，讲如何做到“适度饮食”。
explanation.question: 空前给出 moderation 的定义：只吃身体所需的量，饭后感到满足但不过饱；空后用 But 转折说这并不意味着告别爱吃的食物。
explanation.evidence: You should feel satisfied at the end of a meal, but not too full. ____36____ But it doesn't mean saying goodbye to the foods you love.
explanation.answer: F。空处须承接“适度＝吃得比现在少”，才能与后句 But it doesn't mean… 构成“少吃但不必戒掉爱吃的”的让步转折。D 项“大多数人需要把食量加倍”与全文主旨相反。

Most of us need to double the amount we eat.
Instead, surround yourself with healthy choices.
For many of us, moderation means eating less than we do now.
That won't lead to cheating or giving up on your new eating plan.

explanation.summary: 七选五｜本段小标题 Take your time（慢慢吃）。
explanation.question: 空前说要慢下来、把食物当作营养而非会议间隙的充填物；空后说大脑要几分钟才能告知身体已吃饱，所以要慢吃。
explanation.evidence: rather than just something to eat in between meetings. ____37____ It actually takes a few minutes for your brain to tell your body that it has had enough food
explanation.answer: C。“别在上班路上囫囵吞下一顿饭”正是对上句“别把吃饭挤在会议之间”的具体化，也与下文“慢慢吃”一致。

Most of us need to double the amount we eat.
Instead, surround yourself with healthy choices.
For many of us, moderation means eating less than we do now.

explanation.summary: 七选五｜本段讲“别让不健康零食随手可得”。
explanation.question: 空前说手边备着饼干之类的不健康零食，就更难做到适度。

explanation.answer: E。Instead 与上句的“不健康零食”形成对照，给出正面对策——让自己身边都是健康的选择，是本段收尾的建议。

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节（共20小题；每小题1.5分，满分30分）阅读下面短文，从短文后各题所给的A、B、C和D四个选项中，选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。

passages.label: F
passages.text:
One day, we had a family dinner. While the adults were busy with their serious talk outside, I was left alone in the ____41____ to help my grandmother wash dishes. ____42____ my grandmother would tell me stories about her childhood.

Born just before WWII, my grandmother ____43____ an entirely different childhood lifestyle from mine. She did not have a chance to go to ____44____. Like in typical families, where boys were ____45____ much more than girls, my grandma had to stay at home to do ____46____. The only opportunity (机会) she could seize to ____47____ was when her brother was having Chinese ____48____ with the family tutor. She would sit quietly at the far end of the long dinner table, listening ____49____. This training taught her to read and write her Chinese upside down — a skill that has turned out to be quite ____50____, especially whenever we share the newspaper. On most weekends, my grandmother, a young girl then, and her brother would go to the ____51____. There, they would walk through deep water, sit down cross-legged underwater and hold their ____52____ while they watched all action going on around them. This is something I ____53____ — her ability to open her ____54____ underwater and still sit comfortably on the seabed.

My childhood is quite ____55____ compared with hers. I am ____56____ that I did not need to ____57____ the hardships like she did. I've never faced the problem of ____58____. I guess our different childhood background is what makes my grandmother such an amazing person to ____59____ to: her stories always make my history textbooks ____60____.

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜本文是记叙文，作者通过洗碗时听奶奶讲童年往事，对比两代人的成长境遇。
explanation.question: 句意：大人们在外面聊正事时，我一个人留在厨房帮奶奶洗碗。
explanation.evidence: I was left alone in the ____41____ to help my grandmother wash dishes
explanation.answer: B。洗碗的地点是 kitchen（厨房）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查短语辨析。
explanation.question: 句意：一如往常，奶奶会给我讲她童年的故事。
explanation.evidence: ____42____ my grandmother would tell me stories about her childhood.
explanation.answer: A。谓语用 would（过去反复发生的行为），故用 As always（像往常一样）呼应这种习惯性动作。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词。
explanation.question: 句意：奶奶生于二战前，经历的童年生活方式与我截然不同。
explanation.evidence: Born just before WWII, my grandmother ____43____ an entirely different childhood lifestyle from mine.
explanation.answer: D。与 lifestyle 搭配表示“经历、体验”，用 experienced。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：她没有机会上学。
explanation.evidence: She did not have a chance to go to ____44____.
explanation.answer: B。go to school 上学；下文写她只能趁哥哥上课时偷偷旁听，且末段提到 the problem of education，均可印证。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词。
explanation.question: 句意：就像那些典型的家庭一样，男孩比女孩受偏爱得多。
explanation.evidence: where boys were ____45____ much more than girls, my grandma had to stay at home
explanation.answer: A。be favored 受偏爱、被优待，正解释了女孩只能留在家里干活的原因。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：奶奶只能待在家里做家务。
explanation.evidence: my grandma had to stay at home to do ____46____
explanation.answer: D。do housework 做家务；她没机会上学，故不可能是 homework（作业）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词。
explanation.question: 句意：她唯一能抓住的学习机会，就是哥哥跟家庭教师上中文课的时候。
explanation.evidence: The only opportunity she could seize to ____47____ was when her brother was having Chinese ____48____ with the family tutor.
explanation.answer: B。她无法上学，只能借旁听来 study（学习）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：哥哥正在跟家庭教师上中文课。
explanation.evidence: her brother was having Chinese ____48____ with the family tutor
explanation.answer: C。have lessons with the tutor 跟家教上课；下文 This training（这种训练）亦指上课旁听。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查副词。
explanation.question: 句意：她安静地坐在长餐桌的另一端，专注地听着。
explanation.evidence: She would sit quietly at the far end of the long dinner table, listening ____49____.
explanation.answer: A。listen closely 专心听；正因专注旁听，她才学会了倒着读写汉字。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查形容词。
explanation.question: 句意：这项倒着读写汉字的本领后来相当实用，尤其是我们合看一份报纸的时候。
explanation.evidence: a skill that has turned out to be quite ____50____, especially whenever we share the newspaper
explanation.answer: D。合看报纸时能倒着读，正体现其 practical（实用）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：多数周末，年幼的奶奶会和哥哥去海边。
explanation.evidence: would go to the ____51____. There, they would walk through deep water…still sit comfortably on the seabed
explanation.answer: C。下文出现 deep water、underwater、seabed（海床），可知去的是 beach（海滩）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：他们会走进深水，在水下盘腿坐下、屏住呼吸，看着周围发生的一切。
explanation.evidence: sit down cross-legged underwater and hold their ____52____ while they watched all action going on around them
explanation.answer: B。hold one's breath 屏住呼吸，是水下久坐的必要动作。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词。
explanation.question: 句意：这是我很佩服的一点——她能在水下睁开眼睛，还能舒舒服服地坐在海床上。
explanation.evidence: This is something I ____53____ — her ability to open her ____54____ underwater
explanation.answer: A。破折号后是对这种能力的赞叹，故用 admire（钦佩）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：她能在水下睁开眼睛。
explanation.evidence: her ability to open her ____54____ underwater and still sit comfortably on the seabed
explanation.answer: C。前文说他们在水下 watched all action going on around them，故此处为 open her eyes（睁眼）；又因屏气，不可能张嘴（B）。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查形容词。
explanation.question: 句意：与她相比，我的童年相当幸福。
explanation.evidence: My childhood is quite ____55____ compared with hers. I am ____56____ that I did not need to ____57____ the hardships like she did.
explanation.answer: C。下句说“我不必像她那样经历艰辛”，故我的童年是 happy（幸福的）；开篇已言两人童年 entirely different，故 D 错。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查形容词。
explanation.question: 句意：我很感激自己不必像她那样吃苦。
explanation.evidence: I am ____56____ that I did not need to ____57____ the hardships like she did.
explanation.answer: A。be grateful that… 庆幸、感激，符合作者对比后的心态。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词短语。
explanation.question: 句意：我不必像她那样经历那些艰辛。
explanation.evidence: I did not need to ____57____ the hardships like she did
explanation.answer: B。go through the hardships 经历艰难困苦，为固定搭配。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：我从未面临过教育（上不了学）的问题。
explanation.evidence: I've never faced the problem of ____58____.
explanation.answer: C。回指第二段“奶奶没机会上学、只能偷听哥哥的课”，作者从未遭遇的正是受教育问题。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词。
explanation.question: 句意：正因童年境遇不同，奶奶才成了一个特别值得聊天的人。
explanation.evidence: what makes my grandmother such an amazing person to ____59____ to: her stories always make my history textbooks ____60____
explanation.answer: D。talk to sb. 与某人交谈，与全文“听奶奶讲故事”的情境一致。

explanation.summary: 完形填空｜考查动词短语，本空为全文收束。
explanation.question: 句意：她的故事总能让我的历史课本鲜活起来。
explanation.evidence: her stories always make my history textbooks ____60____
explanation.answer: D。come alive 变得生动、鲜活；奶奶的亲历讲述让书本上的历史有了温度。

sections.partTitle: 第三部分 语言知识运用（共两节，满分45分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节（共10小题；每小题1.5分，满分15分）阅读下面短文，在空白处填入1个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

passages.label: G
passages.text:
Although parks of all sizes and types exist at any level, the national parks, in particular, tend ____61____ (catch) our attention because of their large size and variety. They are ____62____ (treasure) of American heritage (遗产). How did the national park system come about? On a cool, starry night in mid-September 1870, four men relaxed before a campfire along the Firehole River in ____63____ is now northwestern Wyoming. They ____64____ (be) part of a 15-member exploring party that had spent almost five awesome weeks in witness of the natural beauties there.

What should ____65____ (do) with such a beautiful place? They wondered out loud. This area, with ____66____ (it) unique and breathtaking natural beauty, must be well preserved ____67____ all people of the nation to enjoy — as a national park. They all agreed and vowed (承诺) to promote the idea at the ____68____ (complete) of their journey. Their promotional work paid off. Two years later, 18 years before Wyoming became a state, Yellowstone became the first national park in the United States and the world. Yellowstone was the ____69____ (large) United States national park — 2.2 million acres — until Wrangell-Saint Elias in southern Alaska, ____70____ became a national monument in 1978, took the honors as a national park in 1980 with 12.3 million acres.

explanation.summary: 考查非谓语动词｜本文是说明文，讲述美国国家公园体系的由来。
explanation.question: 句意：国家公园因规模大、种类多，格外容易吸引我们的注意。
explanation.evidence: the national parks, in particular, tend ____61____ (catch) our attention
explanation.answer: to catch。tend to do sth. 倾向于做某事，固定用法。

explanation.summary: 考查名词复数。
explanation.question: 句意：它们是美国遗产中的瑰宝。
explanation.evidence: They are ____62____ (treasure) of American heritage
explanation.answer: treasures。主语 They 为复数，表语名词应与之一致，故用复数 treasures。

explanation.summary: 考查名词性从句连接词。
explanation.question: 句意：四个人在如今怀俄明州西北部的火洞河畔篝火旁休息。
explanation.evidence: along the Firehole River in ____63____ is now northwestern Wyoming
explanation.answer: what。介词 in 后是宾语从句，从句缺主语且指“……的地方”，故用 what（= the place which）。

explanation.summary: 考查动词的时态与主谓一致。
explanation.question: 句意：他们是一支 15 人探险队的成员。
explanation.evidence: They ____64____ (be) part of a 15-member exploring party
explanation.answer: were。叙述 1870 年的往事用一般过去时，主语 They 为复数，故用 were。

explanation.summary: 考查被动语态。
explanation.question: 句意：这么美的地方该被怎样处置呢？
explanation.evidence: What should ____65____ (do) with such a beautiful place?
explanation.answer: be done。主语 What 与 do 是被动关系，且情态动词 should 后接动词原形，故用 be done。

explanation.summary: 考查代词。
explanation.question: 句意：这一地区凭借其独特而令人惊叹的自然美景……
explanation.evidence: This area, with ____66____ (it) unique and breathtaking natural beauty
explanation.answer: its。修饰后面的名词短语 natural beauty，需用形容词性物主代词 its。

explanation.summary: 考查介词。
explanation.question: 句意：必须妥善保护起来，供全国人民享用。
explanation.evidence: must be well preserved ____67____ all people of the nation to enjoy
explanation.answer: for。for sb. to do sth. 结构，for 引出不定式的逻辑主语。

explanation.summary: 考查名词。
explanation.question: 句意：他们一致同意，并承诺在旅程结束时推动这一想法。
explanation.evidence: vowed to promote the idea at the ____68____ (complete) of their journey
explanation.answer: completion。at the completion of… 在……完成之时；定冠词 the 与介词 of 之间需用名词。

explanation.summary: 考查形容词最高级。
explanation.question: 句意：黄石一直是美国最大的国家公园——220 万英亩。
explanation.evidence: Yellowstone was the ____69____ (large) United States national park — 2.2 million acres — until…
explanation.answer: largest。定冠词 the + 最高级，表示“在全美国家公园中面积最大”，until 从句说明后来被超越。

explanation.summary: 考查定语从句关系词。
explanation.question: 句意：直到阿拉斯加南部的兰格尔—圣伊莱亚斯（它 1978 年成为国家纪念地）在 1980 年以 1230 万英亩取得国家公园称号。
explanation.evidence: Wrangell-Saint Elias in southern Alaska, ____70____ became a national monument in 1978, took the honors…
explanation.answer: which。非限制性定语从句，先行词为地名（指物），在从句中作主语，故用 which（此处不能用 that）。

sections.partTitle: 第四部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第一节 短文改错（共10小题；每小题1分，满分10分）

questions.stem: 假定英语课上老师要求同桌之间交换修改作文，请你修改你同桌写的以下作文。文中共有10处语言错误，每句中最多有两处。每处错误仅涉及一个单词的增加、删除或修改。
questions.material:
增加：在缺词处加一个漏字符号（∧），并在其下面写出该加的词。
删除：把多余的词用斜线（\）划掉。
修改：在错词下画一横线，并在该词下面写出修改后的词。
注意：1. 每处错误及其修改均仅限一词；
2. 只允许修改10处，多者（从第11处起）不计分。

Last week, I saw a program about Chongqing hotpot on TV. I was curious but planned a special one-day trip there with a friend of me. Our fast train was packing with passengers. A attendant gave us some travel brochures about Chongqing. When we arrived, we went straight a famous restaurant and ordered dishes, which tasted greatly. The atmosphere here made the meal all the more enjoyed. Hotpot is meant for families and friends to sit together, dip everything they like this in one pot, and shared friendship and love.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. 把‘but’改为‘and’
2. 把‘me’改为‘mine’
3. 把‘packing’改为‘packed’
4. 把‘A’改为‘An’
5. 在‘straight’后加上‘to’
6. 把‘greatly’改为‘great’
7. 把‘here’改为‘there’
8. 把‘enjoyed’改为‘enjoyable’
9. 删去‘like 后的 this’
10. 把‘shared’改为‘share’

explanation.summary: 本文是一篇记叙文，作者看了介绍重庆火锅的电视节目后，与朋友专程去重庆吃了一天火锅。

points.note: 「好奇」与「计划前往」是顺承关系，不是转折，故用 and。
a friend of mine 是「双重所有格」的固定结构，of 后须用名词性物主代词。
be packed with 挤满、塞满；主语 train 与 pack 是被动关系。
attendant 以元音音素 /ə/ 开头，须用 An。
go straight to some place 直奔某处；straight 是副词，后接地点须加介词 to。
taste 是系动词，后接形容词作表语，不能用副词。
作者是在回忆重庆之行，叙述立足点不在当地，故用 there 指代那里的氛围。
make + 宾语 + 形容词，修饰物（the meal）表「令人愉快的」，用 enjoyable；enjoyed 表人的感受。
everything they like 已是完整的「先行词＋定语从句」结构，like 的宾语即 everything，再加 this 属多余。
与 sit、dip 并列，同为 for…to 结构中不定式的组成部分，须用动词原形。

sections.partTitle: 第四部分 写作（共两节，满分35分）
sections.secTitle: 第二节 书面表达（满分25分）

questions.stem:
英语课要求做课堂展示，请你根据所给图片，以 Development of Transport in China 为题写一篇发言稿。
注意：
1. 词数100左右；
2. 题目和首句已为你写好。

（图片内容：共享单车、高速列车、新能源汽车三幅示意图）

Development of Transport in China
From the vehicle of horses to today's convenient transport, Chinese transport has an enormous development.
questions.modelAnswer:
Development of Transport in China

From the vehicle of horses to today's convenient transport, Chinese transport has seen enormous development. Chinese transport has undergone remarkable transformations, giving the Chinese people access to different ways of travelling.

Firstly, shared bicycles have emerged as a symbol of urban mobility, offering an affordable and green alternative for short trips. Secondly, the introduction of high-speed trains has dramatically shortened travel times, making intercity travel faster and more comfortable. Lastly, the proliferation of new energy vehicles underscores China's dedication to environmental sustainability, reducing reliance on fossil fuels. These developments illustrate China's journey towards a modern and efficient transportation network that balances convenience with environmental responsibility.

In short, China's transport system is embracing innovation and eco-friendliness.

explanation.summary: 书面表达｜看图作文（发言稿），主题为中国交通的发展，须涵盖图片给出的共享单车、高速列车、新能源汽车三项。
explanation.question: 写作要求：题目与首句已给出，不计入词数；正文 100 词左右。文体为课堂展示的发言稿，可用第三人称客观陈述，时态以现在完成时（体现「发展变化」）为主。结构建议「总—分—总」：首句已总起，中间用 Firstly / Secondly / Lastly 依次点出三种交通方式及其意义，末段一句收束。
explanation.evidence: 词汇积累：共享单车 shared bicycles；高速列车 high-speed trains；新能源汽车 new energy vehicles；城市出行 urban mobility；经济实惠又环保的选择 an affordable and green alternative；大幅缩短 dramatically shorten；普及 proliferation；减少对化石燃料的依赖 reduce reliance on fossil fuels。
explanation.answer: 高分句型：现在完成时 has undergone remarkable transformations 突出「发展」主题；现在分词短语作结果状语 giving the Chinese people access to… / making intercity travel faster… / reducing reliance on fossil fuels（三处结构复现，行文整齐）；定语从句 a modern and efficient transportation network that balances convenience with environmental responsibility。注意首句原文 has an enormous development 搭配不当，范文改为 has seen enormous development（see 表「经历、见证」）。
